title: Kingdom of Sussex
capsule: The Kingdom of Sussex (Sūþseaxna Rīce, 'kingdom of the South Saxons') was one of the early Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of England, occupying the coastal strip south of the Weald between the modern borders of Kent and Hampshire. Its foundation is traditionally attributed to Ælle, said to have landed in 477 CE and to have captured the Roman fort of Anderida (Pevensey) by 491; the Tribal Hidage and early charters document a ruling dynasty through the seventh and eighth centuries. Sussex was the last English kingdom to be converted to Christianity, receiving the bishop Wilfrid at Selsey c.681. The kingdom lost its independence when Offa of Mercia conquered it in 771–772, after which Sussex was ruled by sub-kings under Mercian overlordship and subsequently absorbed into the growing West Saxon hegemony.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's general territory is inferred from the Tribal Hidage and episcopal records; precise boundaries, particularly with Surrey and Kent, are not attested in contemporary documents.
